author: reek
body: This is the fourth endpoint type. Control carries setup packets, bulk carries sectors, interrupt carries keystrokes, and isochronous carries this: a stream with a deadline, where the controller reserves bus bandwidth in advance and a packet that misses its slot is dropped rather than retried. Nothing in the tree drove one before, which is why the camera the emulator has always presented could not be read.

author: reek
body: The streaming interface is class 14 (video), subclass 2 (videostreaming). It appears twice: alt 0 with zero endpoints, alt 1 with the isochronous one. Requiring at least one endpoint is what picks the alternate that can actually stream.

author: reek
body: An isochronous IN endpoint has transfer type 1 in the low two bits of bmAttributes and the direction bit set in its address. The walk stops at the next interface descriptor so it cannot wander into another alternate setting's endpoints.

author: reek
body: SET_INTERFACE is a standard request to the interface recipient: bmRequestType 1, bRequest 11, wValue the alternate setting, wIndex the interface number. Selecting alt 1 is what commits the bandwidth the isochronous endpoint needs.

author: reek
body: One isochronous TRB for the whole frame, then wait for its completion. A short packet is not a failure here: a camera that sends less than a full frame has still sent something, and the residual in the event says how much is missing. Both codes are accepted; anything else is not a frame.

author: reek
body: Pixel accessors, so a caller reads a frame rather than an address. YUYV packs luma per pixel and chroma per pair; this driver exposes the two bytes each pixel occupies and leaves colour conversion to whoever wants a picture.
